newsitem.title: USA: Insurance agents group says backs financial reform.
newsitem.headline: Insurance agents group says backs financial reform.

text.p: The leading trade group for independent insurance agents said Thursday it would no longer oppose legislation allowing banks into the insurance market, as long as states could continue to regulate insurance.
"The old war between the insurance and banking industries is over," Ronald Smith, president of the Independent Insurance Agents of America, said in statement.
The group will support bills in Congress allowing different types of financial services companies to affiliate, Smith said.
Previously the group had opposed financial services integration but changed its position after losing several court cases.

Following a Supreme Court case that freed banks from some of the more onerous state insurance prohibitions, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency announced in November that it would allow national banks to enter non-banking businesses on a case-by-case basis.
The insurance agents group said it favored regulating banks in the insurance market at the state level.
"Clearly recent actions by the OCC have created competitive advantages for national banks," said Robert Rusbuldt, the group's vice president.

"But if legislation is passed that contains true functional regulation of the affected industries, then a level playing field is possible and we can have real competition that benefits all consumers," Rusbuldt said.

House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach, R-Iowa, welcomed the group's new policy. The policy "is a positive signal indicating that prospects for constructive reform are credible in this Congress," Leach said in a statement.
Leach has already introduced a bill permitting financial services integration and providing for state regulation of insurance sales by banks.
The insurance agents' about-face was unanimously approved by the group's board of directors at a meeting over the weekend in Palm Springs.
The group, which represents about 300,000 independent agents, said it plans to meet with Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig in the next 10 days.
